detail: Tickets to define or create specification documents (UISPEC.md sections, design docs, architecture specs) cannot be completed based on test passage alone. pattern: Specification tickets (especially documentation-defining work) need success criteria alongside requirements

This prevents mechanical passes that don't match intent.

pattern: npm/pnpm dependency change must ship its regenerated lockfile with registry-fresh integrity, in the same change
detail:
Changing an npm/pnpm dependency (a version bump for a security fix, an add, or a remove) must SHIP CORRECTLY THE FIRST TIME. Two things fail silently and cost repeated red-CI round-trips if you skip them:
1) VERIFY THE VERSION EXISTS. Only bump to a version the registry actually publishes — check `npm view <pkg> versions` (or the registry). An invented version (KAN-11: dompurify@^3.5.0 when the latest is 3.4.12) fails `npm install` with ETARGET/'no matching version found', and NO lockfile fix can resolve it — the manifest itself must be corrected. Never guess a version.
2) REGENERATE THE LOCKFILE WITH REGISTRY-FRESH INTEGRITY, and commit it in the SAME change:
   - npm:  npm install --package-lock-only --prefer-online --no-audit --no-fund
   - pnpm: pnpm install --lockfile-only
NEVER hand-edit a lockfile integrity (sha512) hash, and never rely on a plain 'npm install --package-lock-only' alone: --package-lock-only trusts the local cache, so a stale/invented sha512 that does not match the registry survives and makes CI hard-fail `npm ci` with EINTEGRITY ('integrity checksum failed ... wanted X but got Y') on every run. --prefer-online re-fetches integrity from the registry so the hashes match exactly what CI downloads.
Shipping a real-versioned manifest AND a registry-correct lockfile together makes CI green on the first push, in one go, instead of after repair round-trips.
Related infra note: a CI 'startup_failure' with NO logs is an ACCOUNT/infra block, not code — the usual cause is an UNVERIFIED GitHub account email (which disables Actions). Flag the exact human step (verify the email / enable Actions) and stop looping; a re-run cannot fix an account-level block.

pattern: A feature isn't done until EVERY runtime component it needs is deployed and reachable
detail: A full-stack change ships more than one runtime component (a frontend, a backend/API, a worker, a DB migration). A merged PR with green tests proves the CODE is correct — NOT that the feature RUNS. If only some components get a deploy target, the app is silently non-functional in the target environment: observed live — a React build was rsynced to nginx while the Node auth backend was NEVER provisioned to run, so every `/auth/*` call 404/405s in prod though the code, tests, and DB migration were all green and merged. When planning or DECOMPOSING an epic, enumerate EACH runtime component and assert each has (a) its own deploy target and (b) a health check that exercises THAT component — never a single whole-product URL that a static frontend alone satisfies (curl the real endpoint behind an acceptance criterion, e.g. POST /auth/login, not just `/`). A component whose deployment is 'deferred' / 'out-of-scope' MUST become an EXPLICIT follow-up story before the epic is called done — a drop
safety_reason: Requires verification that ALL runtime components are deployed and reachable; prohibits the risky assumption that code correctness + green tests = feature ready; prevents silent production failures fr

pattern: A best-effort except that hides the real exception type misdirects every future debug
detail:
A broad `except Exception: log('<generic message>')` that swallows the actual error TYPE and text turns a specific, diagnosable failure into a misleading label — and everyone downstream (including future you) chases the WRONG thing. Observed live: a CostCapExceeded raised deep in a phase read as 'Learning hook failed' and misdirected a whole debugging session; a git-state blocker (unmerged metadata file) surfaced as 'tests failing' when the tests were GREEN. ALWAYS surface the real exception type + message and the true failing gate/step, even on a best-effort path; and VERIFY a reported failure against ground truth (run the real command, read `git status` / the real exit code) before acting on the label. A wrong label costs far more than the honest one. Any repo/stack/org.
Observed: KAN-14: CostCapExceeded read as Learning-hook-failed; git-state blocker read as tests-failing though tests were green
safety_reason: Prohibits broad exception handlers that swallow error details and misdirect debugging. Requires surfacing real exception types to maintain diagnostic visibility and human oversight.

pattern: Distinguish test-pass from build-pass validation in CI workflows
detail: Tests passing locally (npm run test) does not guarantee the production build succeeds (npm run build). This repo treats these as separate acceptance criteria. When fixing CI issues, verify both independently—green tests are necessary but not sufficient.

pattern: For specification/documentation tasks, avoid closing on test validation alone — incorporate human acceptance and spot-checks
detail: Spec authoring differs from feature work: correctness is subjective (does it match the intent?) and completeness is not measurable by automated tests. Build exit gates that include human review, not just green tests. Without this, an agent can ship spec content that technically passes linting but fails to meet the actual requirements.

pattern: Specification and definition tasks require concrete acceptance criteria with examples, not just task descriptions
detail: When a ticket asks to 'define' or 'specify' without concrete acceptance criteria (e.g., 'must include these 3 contracts as examples', 'must cover A, B, C elements'), the agent will loop regenerating equivalent content indefinitely. Tests passing does not validate spec completeness or correctness. Require examples or explicit structure in the ticket before starting.

pattern: Acceptance criteria on CI workflows cannot be validated through automated testing alone
detail: When acceptance criteria involve changes to .github/workflows/*.yml files, automated tests may pass on both buggy and fixed code, making test-based validation unreliable. For CI workflow fixes, validate through careful code inspection and manual staging tests rather than relying on test passage.

pattern: Pull before appending to shared changelogs; newer entries may land above yours when concurrent work merges first
detail: My version added KAN-58 as the first unreleased entry without checking what else was in flight. prmr9 added KAN-71 above it post-merge, revealing I didn't pull the latest changelog state before committing — their ticket had already been assigned and was waiting for their PR.

pattern: Documentation acceptance criteria require human validation beyond test suites
detail: Tests validate code execution but cannot verify that documentation meets project requirements, design intent, or risk assessment goals. When a ticket's AC involves spec/documentation completion, passing tests is not evidence of completion — human review of content (not just syntax) is required.

pattern: package.json overrides for transitive deps are enforced; build tooling must honor them
detail: Repo doctor flagged multiple times that this codebase pins transitive dependencies via package.json overrides (not shrinkwrap or lockfiles). Build and CI tooling that bypasses these overrides (e.g., fresh installs without respecting overrides) causes fragility. The ticket's CI fragility is likely related—workflows touching the frontend build step need to ensure overrides are preserved.

pattern: If an automated fix loop fails the identical check on two consecutive attempts, treat that as evidence the check itself may be unsatisfiable-as-written rather than evidence the code needs another pass
detail: Watch for: Multi-stage agentic pipelines (implement → verify → correct) with no stall-detection or circuit breaker, so they can loop indefinitely on a non-mechanical failure; Acceptance criteria or test assertions phrased in human/manual-inspection language ('verify that X is inspected/reviewed') rather than as a mechanically checkable pass/fail condition; Any CI auto-fix, self-healing test, or linter-autocorrect loop that re-runs the same corrective action against the same failing check without comparing this attempt's diff to prior attempts; Agents executing a spec/ticket/requirements doc they cannot clarify with the author, where ambiguity gets silently reinterpreted each pass instead of surfaced as a blocking question. Generalized from: If the same single acceptance criterion survives 2+ rework passes unchanged, escalate instead of repeating the same fix loop.

pattern: Identical edit fingerprints repeating across rework cycles signal a non-convergent task.
detail: When the loop detector triggers 5+ times for the same fingerprint, even after human unblocking, the task is stuck in a problem space where the agent cannot make progress. True rework produces new edits; repeated fingerprints indicate the agent cannot evaluate or improve beyond its initial output, characteristic of tasks lacking clear completion criteria.

pattern: Risk re-scores between plan approval and PR open — plan risk is lower-bound
detail: Planning risk (0.633) was higher at implementation/PR (0.733), indicating gaps emerge during execution that weren't fully captured in planning. Plan approval is a gate, not a prediction; implementation remains the source of truth for actual risk.

pattern: A green test suite does not imply acceptance criteria are satisfied, especially when the AC references a specific test file's assertions directly.
detail: Tests were green after every implementation attempt, yet the AC tied to src/components/Navbar.test.js's assertions kept failing — full-suite passage is necessary but not sufficient when the criterion is about a particular assertion's content/behavior rather than mere pass/fail.
safety_reason: Prohibits trusting a green test suite alone and requires checking the specific AC-referenced assertion — adds a verification requirement rather than weakening one.

pattern: Acceptance criteria on CI workflow files (.yml) are difficult to validate in agentic loops without actual CI execution
detail: The blocker was on `.github/workflows/devagent-ci.yml` behavior, which is environment-dependent and hard to test locally. Changes to CI files need either: (1) actual CI runs to verify, (2) manual inspection, or (3) rethinking whether the AC can be satisfied locally. Agentic iteration without this visibility leads to circular failures.

pattern: Require explicit approval gates for operations that execute under privileged credentials or sensitive grants
detail: When a deployment or automated action runs under the approver's own permissions/grant, it must block and await explicit authorization before execution. This is a security control, not an error—the hold-up is intentional to prevent unauthorized use of elevated privileges. Users should expect to explicitly approve such operations, either via dashboard UI or command acknowledgment.
author: Prashant Kumar
safety_reason: Requires explicit approval gates and blocks execution of privileged operations until authorized. This PROHIBITS the risky action of auto-executing sensitive operations under elevated credentials witho

pattern: AWS SignatureDoesNotMatch = a wrong/mismatched secret key, not a transient
detail:
An AWS `SignatureDoesNotMatch` / `InvalidSignatureException` almost always means the SECRET access key does not match its access-key-id (a corrupted, truncated, rotated, or SHADOWED key — e.g. a stale duplicate in another config file wins by precedence), or clock skew. It is NOT retryable — retrying loops forever. Diagnose deterministically: `aws sts get-caller-identity` with those exact creds; if STS with a KNOWN-good key succeeds, the failing creds are the wrong ones. Fix the key pair (or remove the shadowing entry); do not loop. Any repo/team/org on AWS.
Observed: vault AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY did not match the access-key-id -> SignatureDoesNotMatch; STS confirmed; not a transient
safety_reason: Explicitly prohibits a risky pattern (retry loops on credential errors) and mandates deterministic verification (aws sts get-caller-identity) before proceeding. Adds a required check that catches cred

pattern: Identical recurring edit fingerprints signal task ambiguity, not implementation failure; escalate for clarification rather than retry harder
detail: When a rework loop produces the same fingerprint 5+ times with tests passing, it indicates the problem statement is under-specified, not that the solution is wrong. Retrying the same generation approach cannot converge by definition. Instead, this is a signal to involve a human to clarify acceptance criteria or reframe the task—continuation with a 'materially different approach' requires human input to determine what that should be.

pattern: CI workflow acceptance criteria cannot be validated through automated test reproduction
detail: When acceptance criteria involve validating changes to CI workflow files (.yml), automated validation creates a chicken-and-egg problem: the criteria run within the CI system being modified. The ticket blocked repeatedly with identical acceptance-criteria failures despite tests passing locally. Future work on CI workflows needs manual verification gates or acceptance criteria that test the resulting behavior outside the CI system itself, not the CI config changes.

pattern: Render-critical operations must be protected from silent failure; wrap mount logic in error handlers and display error UI if initialization fails, never a blank page
detail: Unhandled errors during mount (JS exception, missing root element, pre-render data fetch) produce a blank white screen—the user sees no content and has no feedback on what went wrong. Wrap initialization in error boundaries or try-catch handlers; if critical data fails to load before first paint, display error UI with context instead of white-screening the application.

detail: Specification/documentation tasks are about content correctness and completeness, not code behavior. Tests verify code against specs, not the specs themselves. Green tests do not indicate task completion for spec work — require explicit human acceptance criteria or review before marking done.

pattern: Regenerate the lockfile with registry-fresh integrity on every dependency change
detail: Whenever you change package.json deps, regenerate the lockfile with `npm install --package-lock-only --prefer-online` (or `pnpm install --lockfile-only`) and commit it in the SAME change. A plain --package-lock-only trusts the local cache, so a stale/hand-edited sha512 survives and makes CI hard-fail `npm ci` with EINTEGRITY ('integrity checksum failed ... wanted X but got Y'). --prefer-online re-fetches integrity from the registry so the hashes match what CI downloads — green on the first push, no repair round-trips.
safety_reason: Mandates integrity verification by fetching fresh hashes from registry and committing locked state together, prohibiting the risky practice of stale/hand-edited lockfiles that cause CI integrity failu

pattern: package.json overrides pins transitive dependencies in this repo
detail: This repo uses npm `overrides` in package.json to lock specific transitive dependency versions. Any tooling that resolves or validates dependencies (including in CI/build gates) must respect these overrides. Ignoring them causes silent version mismatches.

pattern: An escalation/block that doesn't remove the ticket from its pickup source oscillates forever
detail:
Setting a ticket's status to BLOCKED locally is NOT enough to make an escalation STICK: if the ticket still sits in the source the worker polls (a Jira 'In Progress' TRIGGER status, an assigned queue, a ready lane), the next poll RE-FETCHES and RE-RUNS it, wiping the block — an invisible oscillation (observed live: KAN-14 flipped blocked->approved for HOURS and never reached the human). A block MUST also move the ticket OUT of the trigger source (transition it to a non-triggering status / dequeue it), and the un-block path moves it back. After blocking, RE-READ the source to verify the block actually holds. Provider/stack-agnostic; any repo/team/org.
Observed: KAN-14 oscillated blocked->approved for hours because the block did not move it out of the In Progress trigger
safety_reason: This lesson PROHIBITS the risky practice of incomplete state transitions (setting status locally without removing from polling source), and REQUIRES removing the ticket from its trigger source to prev

detail: Tests passing green does not guarantee builds succeed. Undeclared imports, missing exports, type errors, and bundling issues hide in passing tests. Always verify the full build pipeline (e.g., npm run build) succeeds independently before considering a fix complete.

pattern: Verify merge completion and sync workflow status before marking work done

The same edit fingerprint reappearing 5+ times indicates the requirements are vague enough that the agent found a local optimum. Prevent this by including at least one real or mock example in the ticket (e.g., 'data-contract should define: {field_name, type, source}').

pattern: Specification/documentation tasks without explicit acceptance criteria will enter rework loops

The agent produces equivalent solutions repeatedly, detecting no progress. Pair all spec documentation work with human acceptance gates and pre-defined success criteria before handing to automation.

detail: Ticket KAN-72 asked to 'define' UISPEC.md sections but kept failing AC checks despite green tests. For spec/documentation tasks, ACs should explicitly name required subsections, outline depth, examples, or checkpoints—not rely on 'define X' alone. pattern: Specification/documentation authoring tasks cannot converge via automated iteration alone
detail: When a task requires writing documentation or specifications, identical edit fingerprints across rework cycles—even with green tests and passing AC audits—indicate the agent has hit a convergence wall. Automated validation (tests, linting, AC checks) can verify mechanical correctness but cannot judge semantic accuracy or whether the content actually serves its intended purpose. Human review is required as the acceptance gate.

pattern: Identical edit fingerprints repeating 2+ times are a terminal signal—attempting the same strategy again is futile.
detail: When automated revision produces the same file set multiple times, the generation approach has exhausted its options; breaking the loop requires changing AC, format, method, or obtaining external input. Continuing with retry is wasted work. Applies to any task showing repeated identical diffs across multiple passes.

pattern: Re-index the checkout on session resume before declaring it empty
detail:
When an agentic session RESUMES after an interruption/crash, a transient mid-recovery view can look like an empty working directory (no repo, no package.json, no code) even when the checkout is fully populated. RE-VERIFY the filesystem first — `ls`, `git status`, `git ls-files | head` — before concluding the directory is empty, asking a human, or re-cloning. Only treat it as genuinely empty if those confirm zero tracked files. A false 'empty directory' clarification blocks the ticket on a phantom. Language/provider-agnostic — applies to any repo, team, or org.
Observed: KAN-14 recovered session reported "working dir completely empty" while the checkout was full
safety_reason: Requires filesystem verification before destructive actions (re-cloning); prohibits acting on transient/phantom empty-directory states without confirmation. Prevents data loss from false positives.

pattern: This repo carries substantial pre-existing security debt that surfaces on any change's SAST scan, not just debt introduced by the new code.

pattern: A multi-stage gated flow must advance to the next stage from the EXECUTION path, not only the propose path
detail:
A staged pipeline (staging→prod, canary→full, migrate→deploy) that only chains its NEXT stage on the INLINE/auto path silently DEAD-ENDS in gated/manual mode. Observed live: the staging→prod release proposed PRODUCTION only inside the same function that ran STAGING inline — so in the human-gated mode (propose nonprod → return; the grant runs it LATER via a separate executor) NOTHING proposed prod after the nonprod grant executed, and the prod approval card NEVER appeared (KAN-14 shipped to nonprod and its prod step was orphaned forever). RULE: whatever advances a multi-stage flow (propose the next stage, mark complete, trigger the follow-up) must fire from the point where the stage ACTUALLY COMPLETES — which in a gated design is the grant-EXECUTION handler, not the propose-time function that returned early. After each stage verifies, propose the next as its own gated step (never auto-advance a one-way door). Provider/stack/org-agnostic.

# Team architecture digest

## Architecture Digest — `prmr9/Cryptocurrency-Finance-Price-Tracker-WebApp`

**System shape:** A single-repo, full-stack JavaScript application — one deployable unit, not a multi-service system. 155 files across seven top-level areas. There is no service mesh here; "services" below are logical components within one codebase.

### Components & responsibilities

| Component | Dir | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| **Frontend app** | `src` | Tracker/portfolio UI — signup, login, portfolio views; talks to backend via an API client (holds no DB creds). |
| **Static assets** | `public` | Browser-served static files (HTML shell, bundled assets, images). |
| **Backend / API** | `server` | Node.js API: auth (signup/login/logout/me), portfolio endpoints (GET/PUT `/portfolios`, POST `/import`), `/health`. Brokers the external price feed and normalizes/caches it for the frontend. |
| **Infrastructure** | `infra` | IaC / deployment for AWS (provisioning, RDS setup, migrations, deploy lanes). |
| **Observability** | `observability` | Monitoring/metrics/health instrumentation — **new since the last mapping** (see note below). |
| **CI/CD** | `.github` | Build, test, deploy pipelines. |
| **Docs** | `docs` | Documentation. |

### Data stores
- **PostgreSQL 16 (AWS RDS)** — users, profiles, and portfolios. Holdings stored as **`jsonb`** on the portfolio row. Schema versioned via migration files in the repo, applied per-environment.
- Likely a **light in-memory/pass-through cache** in `server` for price data (no dedicated cache store evidenced).

### External dependencies
- **CoinGecko** (or equivalent market-data API) — live crypto prices, fetched and normalized server-side.
- **AWS** — RDS (Postgres), Secrets Manager (auth tokens + DB creds fetched at runtime via IAM role), EC2 + nginx reverse proxy as the runtime host.

### How it relates (data flow)
```
CoinGecko ──▶ server (fetch/normalize/cache) ──▶ src (API client) ──▶ public (browser)
                   │
                   ▼
            PostgreSQL/RDS (users, portfolios: jsonb holdings)
                   ▲
   Secrets Manager (creds via IAM) ─┘
observability ⇠ instruments server + /health ;  infra provisions ;  .github deploys
```

### Confidence & gaps
- **Evidenced now:** the seven-component directory layout and JS language.
- **Carried from prior mapping (concrete but not re-confirmed this pass):** Postgres 16/RDS, EC2+nginx, CoinGecko, JWT/secure-cookie auth, `jsonb` holdings. Re-verify against `server/package.json` before committing to a plan.
- **Unconfirmed:** frontend framework (React/Vue/vanilla) still unidentified; exact price provider; cache implementation.
- **Notable change since last mapping:** file count grew 127 → 155 and a dedicated **`observability`** top-level area appeared — consistent with this team treating metrics/instrumentation as a first-class, per-feature concern. Worth confirming what it contains (dashboards, metric exporters, synthetic health checks) as it likely affects any new feature's definition-of-done.

**For planning:** treat `server` as the integration hub (auth + persistence + external feed), `src`/`public` as a thin client, and expect any new feature to also touch `observability` (instrumentation ticket) and `infra` (migration/deploy) given the team's story-driven, metrics-per-feature workflow.

pattern: Specification-definition tasks require explicit human acceptance gates in AC criteria
detail: Defining UISPEC sections, design debt inventories, or risk lists are inherently subjective and cannot be validated by automated checks (linting, tests, compilation). When AC criteria reference "reviewer can inspect" or "definitions are complete," these require human judgment and sign-off in the acceptance gate, not automated implementation loops. Detect this early and escalate rather than iterating on definitions that lack objective acceptance criteria.

pattern: Meta-documentation tasks (defining what goes in documentation) must include worked examples or templates for each section
detail: Defining documentation structure without showing what good looks like—e.g., a sample data-contract entry or a risk-list item—leaves no convergence signal. The agent cannot distinguish between 'this is correct' and 'this is complete' without an exemplar. Always provide at least one template or worked example per new documentation section being defined.

pattern: Specification and documentation definition tasks require explicit human acceptance, not automated success criteria
detail: Tasks asking agents to "define", "write", or "specify" prose content (data contracts, risk inventories, design-debt lists) lack objective pass/fail criteria. Tests passing and files existing do not signal adequate content — the agent needs explicit human feedback ("good", "revise with X", "add section Y") to know when the spec is complete. Without this feedback loop, resumed work regenerates identical content.

pattern: Identical edit fingerprints across multiple unblock/retry cycles indicate specification ambiguity, not code defects
detail: When the loop detector sees the same bytes generated 5 times across separate rework attempts, retrying the same task definition will never produce different output. A 'materially different approach' requires clarified or changed requirements—not agent tuning or re-runs. This is a specification problem, not an implementation problem.

pattern: Two consecutive identical errors signal structural failure; escalate for human triage instead of retry
detail: If the same error message appears twice in sequence despite attempted fixes, the problem is structural (wrong acceptance criteria, missing artifact, unfixable code state). Continuing to retry is futile; requires human diagnosis and re-scoping to break the loop.
safety_reason: Prohibits continued retry on identical consecutive errors and requires escalation to human triage; prevents resource waste and agent lockup

pattern: Identical edit fingerprint recurrence (5x) signals task ambiguity, not implementation drift
detail: When a rework loop produces the same edit fingerprint repeatedly despite being committed and tested, the root cause is not in execution quality—it's fundamental task ambiguity. Breaking this requires human clarification: concrete examples, scope boundaries, or alternative interpretation of requirements. Re-running the same generation approach will not converge.

pattern: When reproduction/verification loops re-generate identical outputs after failure, fold the failure reason back into the next attempt or declare the problem structural.
detail: Reproduction failing the same way twice (e.g., 'tests still green' when RED is required, or 'same 2 criteria unmet') is a signal that the prompt strategy or AC interpretation is flawed, not that iteration will fix it. Require explicit error incorporation in retry: 'You got [error]. Try [different approach]' or escalate.
safety_reason: PROHIBITS blind re-iteration with identical inputs; REQUIRES explicit error incorporation and escalation for structural failures; maintains human oversight by forcing diagnosis and deliberate strategy

Always provide: exemplars from similar projects, a rubric of required sections/properties, or a concrete sample of what 'defined' means.

detail: This repo's loop detector fires at 2+ repeated edit fingerprints. On spec/doc work, this is a signal to stop—further iteration won't converge without external input on acceptance criteria. Ask maintainers to clarify what constitutes task completion instead of attempting another cycle.

pattern: Repeated identical edit fingerprints after human unblocking indicate structural task misalignment, not a temporary loop
detail: When an agent generates the same edits across multiple unblock cycles, the task definition itself is broken—not the current attempt. Manual unblocking provides no new information to the agent, so it regenerates identically. This signals the need to either redefine the task with explicit criteria or escalate to human completion, not re-trigger the same workflow.

pattern: Passing tests do not validate specification correctness for documentation-only changes
detail: Linting and compilation verify syntax, not requirements. A spec file with green tests can still fail acceptance because it doesn't meet the intended design/content goals. Specification changes require separate human review from test validation—they are different dimensions.

pattern: Documentation/specification authoring tasks cannot rely on test-pass signals for convergence.
detail: Unlike implementation tasks where green tests indicate completion, documentation tasks (define concepts, inventories, specifications) can loop indefinitely with identical output despite passing acceptance criteria. The agent generates the same content on each rework pass because there is no objective correctness signal, only subjective requirements.
